reviews.justification: Both rows are shards of a single enumerated first-line smoking-cessation pharmacotherapy choice, and naming NRT versus bupropion changes the exemplar drug, not the tested decision, since both are equally acceptable first-line answers.
Both rows demand the same bundled immediate response to malignant hyperthermia, and the differing stage and family labels reflect metadata inconsistency rather than a second scoreable action.
The generic row and the NRT row test the same single choice of first-line smoking-cessation pharmacotherapy, with the second simply naming one correct realization of that choice.

Row A is a bare restatement of the study unit and therefore functions as a diagnostic heading that spans several ileus decisions, one of which is the specific separation of ileus from mechanical obstruction in row B.
Row A names one concrete preventive bundle against intraoperative heat loss, while row B is an undifferentiated hypothermia heading covering the unit's preventive decisions generally.

Row A restates the unit name as a heading over the whole initial prenatal encounter, whereas row B pins down the specific enumeration of baseline history, examination, and first-trimester investigations.
Row A is a generic arrest heading for the unit, while row B tests the specific act of entering the corresponding resuscitation algorithm, which is one component of that heading.
Row A tests one focused differentiation centred on early Alzheimer disease, whereas row B is a bare dementia heading covering the unit's broader differential reasoning.
Row A names a single specific topical agent, while row B is the general first-line management selection for the unit, which encompasses more than that one agent.
Row A tests a defined criteria-based diagnosis of depression in primary care, while row B is an unqualified depression heading in the screening family that spans additional preventive decisions.
Row A is limited to the common primary-care sleep diagnoses, whereas row B is a bare heading for sleep disorders generally, including conditions outside that restricted set.
Row A merely restates the unit as a diagnostic heading, while row B isolates the specific duration- and severity-based separation of bacterial from viral disease within it.
Row A is a management heading for the whole unit, whereas row B tests the particular patient-factor-driven choice among first-line treatment modalities.

Both rows scope to diagnosing growth hormone deficiency within the same unit, and the extra naming of the biochemical and provocative testing path in row B is an evidence route to the same decision rather than a second decision.

The two rows describe severity-driven psoriasis therapy in very similar terms, but row B is tagged as an emergency stabilization decision, so I cannot establish that they encode one and the same scoreable decision.
Row A restricts the diagnostic task to the primary-care presentation dominated by uncomplicated cystitis, while row B is an unrestricted dysuria heading covering the wider diagnostic field.

Row A is a general heading for acute atrial fibrillation management, which contains additional decisions such as anticoagulation, while row B tests only the choice between immediate cardioversion and pharmacologic rate or rhythm control.

Row A is a catch-all heading for pediatric considerations in this unit, whereas row B tests the specific recognition of the family as the unit of care and of developmental capacity as the basis of decisional authority.
Varenicline and nicotine replacement are alternative correct answers to the single first-line smoking-cessation pharmacotherapy choice, so the two rows realize one decision rather than two.
Row A names one specific injectable therapy, while row B is the general first-line management selection for the unit and covers the full set of candidate treatments.

Topical antiperspirants and injected botulinum toxin sit at different rungs of the hyperhidrosis treatment ladder with different indications and consequences, so each supports its own scoreable management decision.

Choosing cross-sectional imaging and choosing functional imaging for a pulmonary nodule are different investigation pathways triggered by different nodule characteristics, which the contract treats as separate decisions.
Row A names one acceptable agent for the very decision row B states generically, so the two express a single first-line pharmacotherapy choice in different ways.
Row A is a bare hypertension heading spanning the unit's diagnostic reasoning, while row B tests the specific criteria-based confirmation of the diagnosis.
